structure_and_depth.basis: Continuous reading 1-80,81-155,156-219 against task and effective requirements. The report distinguishes datasets, frameworks, execution harnesses and leaderboards before tracing HELM version changes and what its aggregate measures. Its complementary matrix selects distinct failure modes rather than double-counting overlapping datasets. Worked interpretations explain prompt interventions, EvalPlus rank reversal, changed repository task populations, tau weighting/pass metrics and verbosity-sensitive preference scores. The reproducibility tables identify disclosed model, prompt, scorer and sample conditions as well as unresolved run identities and historical dependency access; they distinguish procedure inspection, rescoring and new inference. Exposure, evaluator defects and finite-sample uncertainty lead to different remedies. The two deployment sections connect these mechanisms to policy grounding/action correctness versus repository navigation/maintained behavior, and include contrary human-productivity evidence without extrapolating a universal multiplier. Relevant originals checked: HELM Capabilities MB03:105-124 on aggregation/judging/extraction, EvalPlus MB10:179-183 and 380-386 on changed coverage/rank, tau2 MB20:3-10 and 21-25 on version incompatibility. The recommendations follow those concrete comparisons, with successful-task cost and operational evidence as conditions rather than a universal winning model. No necessary structure/depth correction found; full historical benchmark reproduction and exhaustive source verification were outside this perspective.
